svg.title: Annex A5 · Daily update: official sources, series and signals
svg.desc: The daily update: triggers, build job preparation, reading ENFEN and its technical report, NOAA, IGP and IMARPE, series, GRD signal, freshness and incidents.
svg.text: Annex A5 · Daily update: official sources, series and signals

observatory.yml runs the Python pipeline (python -m enso.observatory) every night at 23:37 Lima and whenever someone asks. It reads each official source, validates, builds the series and statuses and logs every problem. News
and places are in annex A6; publication, in A8.
Details these boxes of the full diagram: Daily update (observatory.yml), Official source reading, Series, statuses and GRD signal, Incident log, Reference data: places and thresholds.
GitHub Actions · one run at a time

g.title: 1. Every night 23:37 Lima → Queue: scheduled. The nightly run.
2. Merge to main or by hand → Queue: merge or by hand. A change on main is published right away.
3. enso-refresh → Queue: a new copy exists. No need to wait for 23:37 to use the Peru copy or an uploaded PDF.
4. Watchdog → Queue: site behind. Unless a run is in progress or one was relaunched in the last 6 h.
5. Queue → Tests: the build job starts. If a run is already going, the new one waits its turn.
6. Tests → Site address: tests pass. Without green tests it does not go on.
7. Site address → Copies and history: address resolved. The address decides where the previous publication and the corrections are read from.
8. Copies and history → python -m enso.observatory: copy folders. The folders go even if empty: the pipeline knows what is missing and logs it.
9. python -m enso.observatory → Critical first: reads the sources. 8 minutes for all official sources.
10. Critical first → Latest ENFEN communiqué: ENFEN communiqués. The communiqué listing, with its fallback ladder.
11. Latest ENFEN communiqué → Technical report: current communiqué. The report is chosen by date, not number, and downloaded only once.
12. Technical report → Optional second reading: the reader fails. The model's proposal waits for review; it is never published on its own.
13. Critical first → NOAA, IGP and IMARPE: the other 14 sources. NOAA, the ICEN and IMARPE's bulletin, each with its reader.
14. NOAA, IGP and IMARPE → Format fingerprint: parsed data. With their format fingerprint and range warnings.
15. Format fingerprint → Series and statuses: valid or carried. Each source brings its fresh value or the last good one, with its real date.
16. Reference data → Series and statuses: thresholds and categories. Categories and the signal come from Python; the browser only adds reading aids.
17. Series and statuses → GRD signal: latest values. The signal uses OISST, winds, D20 and SOI.
18. GRD signal → Freshness of each value: status by indicator. Everything goes through freshness before being published.
19. Format fingerprint → Incident log: each stage's problems. format-drift, format-changed, unreachable, carried-forward and the health of the copies.
Every night 23:37 Lima. cron 37 4 * * * (04:37 UTC; Peru has no daylight saving).
Merge to main or by hand. Every push to main publishes (except changes only in .md or docs/). By hand you choose whether to ask the Internet Archive for new copies.

g.title: Site address. DEPLOY_TARGET picks GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages; with Cloudflare the address comes from the project and place corrections from /api/geo/overrides. Technology: cloudflare_pages.py.

g.title: Copies and history. Fetches data-peru, data-n8n and data-manual, the news-history copy from data-archive and the reader-feed state. If something is missing, it goes on and logs it. Technology: git, gh api, actions/cache.

a.title: Annex A4: Download in GitHub Actions and per-source fallbacks

g.title: python -m enso.observatory. --out public/data, --previous ${SITE_URL}data, the copies, the history and --fail-on critical. 26 min limit. Technology: Python 3.12, httpx.
Critical first. ENFEN, ICEN and the ENSO discussion go first: a bad NOAA day does not leave the communiqué unread. Then the other 14 sources, each with its fallback ladder.

g.title: Latest ENFEN communiqué. Joins the portal listing, the DHN mirror and the API; probes the numbers after the latest known one (up to 6) and reads the PDF: number, status, level, dates, summary and outlook by region. Technology: pypdf, feeds/peru.py.

g.title: Technical report. Once per communiqué (10 to 20 MB): provisional ICEN and monthly probabilities, with page and quote. Validated with a schema, sums to 100 % and IGP's ICEN; if no route brings it, it waits in the console. Technology: reports.py.

g.title: NOAA, IGP and IMARPE. Readers by headers, not positions: CPC and PSL text, the ENSO discussion in HTML, the ICEN, GODAS D20 (HTTP range of the GRIB) and IMARPE's bulletin (Sundays). Technology: cpc.py, godas.py, imarpe_bsobp.py.

g.title: Format fingerprint. Each reader returns a fingerprint (headers, columns, pattern). If it changes from yesterday, format-drift; if it can no longer be read, FormatChanged and the value is not published.

g.title: Reference data. ICEN categories (ENFEN Technical Note 01-2024), GRD team thresholds (transcribed draft), UBIGEO and IGN boundaries. Technology: YAML, JSON.

Series and statuses. 23 series with latest value, age and category, the weekly data by Niño region, the ENFEN and NOAA statuses and ICEN events (+0.5 or −0.7 for at least 3 months). Technology: Builder, signals.py.
